Problem Domain:
Customer Relationship Management (CRM), IT Service Management (ITSM), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning Classification, Operations Optimization.

Project Description:
This project develops an intelligent system to automatically prioritize incoming customer support tickets based on their textual content and associated metadata. The goal is to reduce manual triage effort, ensure critical issues are addressed promptly, and improve overall customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. The system utilizes Pandas for managing ticket data (including text, timestamps, customer information, etc.). State-of-the-art NLP embeddings, generated using libraries like Sentence-Transformers (built on Hugging Face Transformers), are used to capture the semantic meaning of the ticket descriptions. These embeddings, potentially combined with other engineered features from metadata (e.g., customer tier, issue type category, time since creation), are fed into a robust machine learning classifier, specifically a Random Forest Classifier from Scikit-learn, trained to predict the appropriate priority level (e.g., Low, Medium, High, Urgent).

Frameworks Used:

  • Core Data: Pandas, NumPy
  • NLP Embeddings: Sentence-Transformers (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2, paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2)
  • Machine Learning: Scikit-learn (RandomForestClassifier, train_test_split, StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder, classification_report, confusion_matrix)
  • Text Preprocessing (Basic): regex (optional, for cleaning before embedding if needed)
  • Data Simulation (Optional): Faker (for generating realistic-looking text and metadata)
  • Configuration: YAML
  • Model Persistence: Joblib or native Scikit-learn/Sentence-Transformer saving methods.

Dataset:
Real customer support ticket datasets with accurate priority labels are highly sensitive and rarely public. We will simulate a dataset for demonstration purposes.

  • Characteristics: The simulated dataset will include:
    • ticket_id: Unique identifier.
    • creation_timestamp: Time the ticket was created.
    • customer_id: Identifier for the customer.
    • customer_tier: Categorical (e.g., Free, Basic, Premium, Enterprise).
    • subject: Short summary/title of the issue.
    • description: Detailed text describing the problem.
    • priority: The target variable (e.g., 1-Low, 2-Medium, 3-High, 4-Urgent) - this will be assigned based on simulated keywords or patterns in the description/subject and customer tier.
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import logging
import os
from faker import Faker
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Optional, List

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s")

# --- Simulate Support Ticket Data ---
def simulate_support_tickets(num_tickets: int = 5000, 
                             output_path: Optional[str] = "./data/simulated_support_tickets.csv") -> Optional[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Generates a DataFrame simulating customer support tickets with priorities."""
    logging.info(f"Simulating {num_tickets} support tickets...")
    fake = Faker()
    Faker.seed(42)
    np.random.seed(42)

    data = []
    customer_tiers = ["Free", "Basic", "Premium", "Enterprise"]
    tier_weights = [0.3, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1]
    priorities = [1, 2, 3, 4] # Low, Medium, High, Urgent

    # Keywords associated with priorities (simplified simulation logic)
    urgent_keywords = ["down", "critical", "outage", "cannot access", "urgent", "blocker", "production issue", "system unavailable"]
    high_keywords = ["error", "bug", "slow", "failing", "broken", "unable to use", "performance degradation", "security concern"]
    medium_keywords = ["question", "how to", "feature request", "minor issue", "clarification", "documentation", "login problem"]

    start_date = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=180)

    for i in range(num_tickets):
        ticket_id = f"TKT-{10000 + i}"
        timestamp = fake.date_time_between(start_date=start_date, end_date="now")
        customer_id = f"CUST-{fake.random_int(min=100, max=999)}"
        customer_tier = np.random.choice(customer_tiers, p=tier_weights)

        # Generate text and determine priority based on keywords and tier
        priority = 1 # Default to Low
        subject = ""
        description = ""

        # Higher chance of higher priority for higher tiers
        base_priority_roll = np.random.rand()
        if customer_tier == "Enterprise" and base_priority_roll < 0.4: priority = 4
        elif customer_tier == "Enterprise" and base_priority_roll < 0.7: priority = 3
        elif customer_tier == "Premium" and base_priority_roll < 0.2: priority = 4
        elif customer_tier == "Premium" and base_priority_roll < 0.5: priority = 3
        elif customer_tier == "Basic" and base_priority_roll < 0.3: priority = 3

        # Override/Increase priority based on keywords
        keyword_roll = np.random.rand()
        if keyword_roll < 0.15: # Chance of urgent keywords
             kw = np.random.choice(urgent_keywords)
             subject = f"{kw.capitalize()} in {fake.bs()}"
             description = f"Help! The system is {kw}. We are experiencing a major {fake.bs()} problem. {fake.paragraph(nb_sentences=3)}"
             priority = 4
        elif keyword_roll < 0.40: # Chance of high priority keywords
             kw = np.random.choice(high_keywords)
             subject = f"Issue with {fake.bs()}: {kw}"
             description = f"I encountered an {kw} when trying to {fake.bs()}. It seems {kw}. Details: {fake.paragraph(nb_sentences=4)}"
             priority = max(priority, 3)
        elif keyword_roll < 0.75: # Chance of medium priority keywords
             kw = np.random.choice(medium_keywords)
             subject = f"{kw.capitalize()} about {fake.bs()}"
             description = f"I have a {kw} regarding the {fake.bs()} feature. {fake.paragraph(nb_sentences=2)} Could you please provide guidance?"
             priority = max(priority, 2)
        else: # Low priority / generic
             subject = f"Inquiry about {fake.bs()}"
             description = f"Hello, I was wondering about {fake.bs()}. {fake.paragraph(nb_sentences=3)} Thanks."
             priority = max(priority, 1)

        data.append({
            "ticket_id": ticket_id,
            "creation_timestamp": timestamp,
            "customer_id": customer_id,
            "customer_tier": customer_tier,
            "subject": subject,
            "description": description,
            "priority": priority
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(data)
    df[    creation_timestamp  ] = pd.to_datetime(df[  creation_timestamp  ])
    logging.info(f"Generated simulated tickets. Shape: {df.shape}")

    # Save if path provided
    if output_path:
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)
            df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
            logging.info(f"Saved simulated tickets to {output_path}")
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to save simulated tickets: {e}")

    return df

# Generate or load the data
SIMULATED_TICKETS_PATH = "./data/simulated_support_tickets.csv"
if os.path.exists(SIMULATED_TICKETS_PATH):
    logging.info(f"Loading simulated tickets from {SIMULATED_TICKETS_PATH}")
    tickets_df = pd.read_csv(SIMULATED_TICKETS_PATH, parse_dates=[    creation_timestamp  ])
else:
    tickets_df = simulate_support_tickets(output_path=SIMULATED_TICKETS_PATH)

if tickets_df is not None:
    print("Sample Simulated Support Ticket Data:")
    print(tickets_df.head())
    print("\nData Info:")
    tickets_df.info()
    print("\nPriority Distribution:")
    print(tickets_df[    priority    ].value_counts(normalize=True).sort_index())
else:
    print("Failed to load or generate simulated ticket data.")

Use Cases:

  1. Automated Ticket Triage: Automatically assign an initial priority to incoming tickets, routing them to the appropriate support queue or team.
  2. Workload Balancing: Help distribute high-priority tickets effectively among support agents.
  3. SLA Monitoring: Identify tickets at risk of breaching Service Level Agreements (SLAs) based on predicted priority and age.
  4. Early Warning System: Flag potentially critical issues based on text analysis even before manual review.
  5. Trend Analysis: Analyze the types of issues associated with different priority levels to identify recurring problems or areas for product improvement.
  6. Agent Assistance: Provide agents with a predicted priority score as guidance during manual review.

Full Development Lifecycle (Corporate View):

  1. Requirements & Goal Definition (3-5 weeks): Define priority levels and their business impact. Identify key factors influencing priority (text content, customer value, product area, keywords). Specify desired model performance (accuracy, precision/recall for high-priority tickets). Determine integration points with existing ticketing systems (e.g., Zendesk, Jira Service Management, Salesforce Service Cloud).
  2. Data Collection & Preparation (4-7 weeks): Extract historical ticket data (text, metadata, reliable historical priority labels assigned by humans). Clean and preprocess text data (handle HTML, code snippets, PII redaction). Engineer features from metadata (e.g., time since creation, customer tenure, previous ticket history).
  3. NLP Embedding Strategy (3-4 weeks): Select an appropriate pre-trained Sentence-Transformer model based on performance, computational cost, and domain relevance. Generate embeddings for the ticket descriptions (or combined subject+description).
  4. Feature Engineering & Selection (4-6 weeks): Combine text embeddings with processed metadata features. Handle categorical features (e.g., customer tier) using one-hot encoding. Scale numerical features. Perform feature selection if the combined feature space is very large.
  5. Model Training & Tuning (6-9 weeks): Split data into training, validation, and test sets. Train a Random Forest Classifier (or other suitable models like Gradient Boosting, SVM, Logistic Regression). Tune hyperparameters using techniques like GridSearchCV or RandomizedSearchCV. Address potential class imbalance in priority levels (e.g., using class weights, over/under-sampling techniques like SMOTE).
  6. Evaluation & Validation (3-5 weeks): Evaluate the model on the test set using relevant metrics (overall accuracy, precision/recall/F1 per priority level, confusion matrix). Analyze model errors and biases. Validate performance against business requirements.
  7. Integration & Deployment (5-8 weeks): Develop an API or service to expose the model for prediction. Integrate the service with the ticketing system to automatically assign priorities to new tickets or provide suggestions to agents. Deploy the model using appropriate infrastructure (cloud functions, containerized service).
  8. Monitoring & Retraining (Ongoing): Monitor model performance in production (prediction accuracy, drift in data distributions). Collect feedback from support agents on prediction quality. Retrain the model periodically with new labeled data to maintain accuracy and adapt to evolving language and issues.

# --- Filename: support_ticket_prioritization.py ---

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import logging
import os
import time
import yaml
import joblib
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional, Any

# NLP Embeddings
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

# Machine Learning
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, accuracy_score

# Configuration
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(module)s - %(message)s")

# --- Constants & Config ---
# Data Config (using simulated data path from above)
INPUT_DATA_PATH = "./data/simulated_support_tickets.csv"
TEXT_COLS = ["subject", "description"] # Columns to combine for embedding
METADATA_COLS_CAT = ["customer_tier"] # Categorical metadata
METADATA_COLS_NUM = ["ticket_age_hours"] # Numerical metadata (engineered)
TARGET_COL = "priority"

# Model Config
EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2" # Efficient and good quality
TEST_SIZE = 0.2
RANDOM_STATE = 42
# RF Hyperparameters (example - tune these)
RF_N_ESTIMATORS = 200 
RF_MAX_DEPTH = 15
RF_MIN_SAMPLES_SPLIT = 10
RF_MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF = 5
RF_CLASS_WEIGHT = "balanced" # Handle potential imbalance

# Paths
OUTPUT_DIR = "./models/ticket_priority"
PIPELINE_PATH = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "priority_pipeline.joblib")
EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "embedding_model") # Save separately if needed

# --- Feature Engineering ---
def engineer_features(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Engineers features like ticket age."""
    logging.info("Engineering features...")
    df_eng = df.copy()
    # Calculate ticket age in hours (relative to the most recent ticket for consistency)
    if not df_eng[    creation_timestamp  ].empty:
         latest_time = df_eng[    creation_timestamp  ].max()
         df_eng[    ticket_age_hours    ] = (latest_time - df_eng[  creation_timestamp  ]).dt.total_seconds() / 3600
         # Handle potential negative ages if data spans future?
         df_eng[    ticket_age_hours    ] = df_eng[ ticket_age_hours    ].clip(lower=0)
    else:
         df_eng[    ticket_age_hours    ] = 0

    # Combine text fields
    df_eng[    combined_text   ] = df_eng[TEXT_COLS].fillna("").agg(       .join, axis=1)

    logging.info(f"Added features: {[    ticket_age_hours    ,   combined_text   ]}")
    return df_eng

# --- Main Execution Logic ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.info("--- Starting Support Ticket Prioritization Pipeline --- ")
    start_pipeline_time = time.time()

    # Load data
    if not os.path.exists(INPUT_DATA_PATH):
        logging.error(f"Input data not found at {INPUT_DATA_PATH}. Run simulation first.")
        exit()
    input_df = pd.read_csv(INPUT_DATA_PATH, parse_dates=[    creation_timestamp  ])
    logging.info(f"Input data loaded. Shape: {input_df.shape}")

    # Drop rows with missing priority
    input_df.dropna(subset=[TARGET_COL], inplace=True)
    input_df[TARGET_COL] = input_df[TARGET_COL].astype(int)
    logging.info(f"Data shape after dropping NA priorities: {input_df.shape}")

    # Engineer Features
    df_processed = engineer_features(input_df)

    # --- Generate Text Embeddings ---
    logging.info(f"Loading sentence transformer model: {EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME}")
    embedding_model = SentenceTransformer(EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME)

    # Save the embedding model (optional, if not easily reloadable by name)
    # os.makedirs(EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    # embedding_model.save(EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR)

    logging.info("Generating text embeddings (this may take time)...")
    embedding_start_time = time.time()
    # Ensure text is string type, handle potential NaN/None
    texts_to_embed = df_processed[    combined_text   ].astype(str).tolist()
    text_embeddings = embedding_model.encode(texts_to_embed, show_progress_bar=True)
    embedding_end_time = time.time()
    logging.info(f"Embeddings generated. Shape: {text_embeddings.shape}. Time: {embedding_end_time - embedding_start_time:.2f}s")

    # Combine embeddings with metadata
    # Create a DataFrame for embeddings
    embedding_cols = [f"embed_{i}" for i in range(text_embeddings.shape[1])]
    embeddings_df = pd.DataFrame(text_embeddings, index=df_processed.index, columns=embedding_cols)

    # Select metadata features
    metadata_df = df_processed[METADATA_COLS_CAT + METADATA_COLS_NUM]

    # Concatenate features
    features_df = pd.concat([metadata_df, embeddings_df], axis=1)
    logging.info(f"Combined features DataFrame shape: {features_df.shape}")

    # Target variable
    y = df_processed[TARGET_COL]

    # --- Train/Test Split ---
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        features_df, y, test_size=TEST_SIZE, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, stratify=y
    )
    logging.info(f"Train/Test split complete. Train shape: {X_train.shape}, Test shape: {X_test.shape}")

    # --- Build Preprocessing and Model Pipeline ---
    # Preprocessor for metadata: Scale numerical, OneHotEncode categorical
    numeric_transformer = Pipeline(steps=[(    scaler  , StandardScaler())])
    categorical_transformer = Pipeline(steps=[(    onehot  , OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown= ignore  ))])

    # Use ColumnTransformer to apply different transformers to different columns
    # Note: Embeddings are already numerical, but scaling them *might* sometimes help RF, though often unnecessary.
    # Let's assume embeddings don't need scaling for RF.
    preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
        transformers=[
            (    num , numeric_transformer, METADATA_COLS_NUM),
            (    cat , categorical_transformer, METADATA_COLS_CAT),
            # Pass through embedding columns (all remaining columns)
            (    passthrough_embed   ,   passthrough , embedding_cols)
        ],
        remainder=    drop     # Drop any columns not specified
    )

    # Create the full pipeline with preprocessing and classifier
    pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[
        (    preprocessor    , preprocessor),
        (    classifier  , RandomForestClassifier(
            n_estimators=RF_N_ESTIMATORS,
            max_depth=RF_MAX_DEPTH,
            min_samples_split=RF_MIN_SAMPLES_SPLIT,
            min_samples_leaf=RF_MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF,
            class_weight=RF_CLASS_WEIGHT,
            random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
            n_jobs=-1 # Use all available cores
        ))
    ])

    # --- Train the Pipeline ---
    logging.info("Training the Random Forest pipeline...")
    train_start_time = time.time()
    pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
    train_end_time = time.time()
    logging.info(f"Pipeline training finished. Time: {train_end_time - train_start_time:.2f}s")

    # --- Evaluate the Pipeline ---
    logging.info("Evaluating the pipeline on the test set...")
    y_pred = pipeline.predict(X_test)

    accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
    report = classification_report(y_test, y_pred)
    matrix = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)

    logging.info(f"Test Set Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
    logging.info("Classification Report:\n" + report)
    logging.info("Confusion Matrix:\n" + str(matrix))

    # --- Save the Pipeline ---
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump(pipeline, PIPELINE_PATH)
    logging.info(f"Trained pipeline saved to {PIPELINE_PATH}")

    # --- Example Prediction (on a sample from test set) ---
    logging.info("\n--- Example Prediction ---")
    sample_idx = X_test.index[:5] # Take first 5 samples from test set index
    sample_features = X_test.loc[sample_idx]
    sample_actual = y_test.loc[sample_idx]
    sample_pred = pipeline.predict(sample_features)
    sample_proba = pipeline.predict_proba(sample_features)

    # Get original text for context
    sample_orig_text = df_processed.loc[sample_idx][[    subject ,   description ]]

    print("Sample Predictions:")
    for i, idx in enumerate(sample_idx):
        print(f"\nTicket Index: {idx}")
        print(f"  Subject: {sample_orig_text.loc[idx,     subject ]}")
        # print(f"  Description: {sample_orig_text.loc[idx,     description ][:100]}...") # Truncate description
        print(f"  Actual Priority: {sample_actual.loc[idx]}")
        print(f"  Predicted Priority: {sample_pred[i]}")
        print(f"  Prediction Probabilities: {np.round(sample_proba[i], 3)}")

    end_pipeline_time = time.time()
    logging.info(f"--- Pipeline finished in {end_pipeline_time - start_pipeline_time:.2f} seconds --- ")

Where to Go From Here (Improvements):

  1. Hyperparameter Optimization: Use GridSearchCV or RandomizedSearchCV with cross-validation to find the optimal hyperparameters for the RandomForestClassifier and potentially the preprocessor steps.
  2. Advanced Text Preprocessing: Implement more sophisticated text cleaning tailored to support tickets (e.g., removing signatures, quoted replies, code block handling).
  3. Alternative Embeddings/Models: Experiment with different Sentence-Transformer models or even fine-tune a Transformer model directly on the ticket classification task (potentially more complex but could yield higher accuracy).
  4. Feature Engineering: Engineer more informative features from timestamps (e.g., time of day, day of week), customer history (e.g., number of previous tickets, average past priority), or text (e.g., TF-IDF scores for specific keywords in addition to embeddings).
  5. Handling Class Imbalance: Explore more advanced techniques for handling imbalanced priority classes, such as SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) within the pipeline or using cost-sensitive learning algorithms.
  6. Explainability (XAI): Use tools like SHAP or LIME to understand which features (text embedding dimensions or metadata) are most influential in the model's priority predictions for specific tickets.
  7. Confidence Scoring: Use the predict_proba output to assess the model's confidence and potentially flag low-confidence predictions for manual review.
  8. Multi-Label Classification: If tickets can belong to multiple categories or require multiple tags, adapt the model to a multi-label classification framework.
  9. Online Learning / Drift Detection: Implement mechanisms to detect drift in the incoming ticket data or model performance over time and trigger retraining or alerts.
  10. User Feedback Loop: Build a mechanism for support agents to provide feedback on incorrect predictions, which can be used to improve future model retraining cycles.
